guides.title: Five upgrades for a website with personality, and real 3D
guides.description: Choose visual direction, real 3D, polish, motion or browser checks. Start with the task your page needs.
guides.cardSummary: A complete Codex handoff, a real 3D route and checks that matter.
requirements: A website project you can safely edit
Browser and an appropriate Three.js renderer
guides.intro: A distinctive site starts with clear choices. Use design guidance to settle the visual system, a dedicated Three.js skill for a real scene, and focused checks before adding more tools. These are independent options, not an install-everything bundle.

sections.title: Match the upgrade to the work
sections.html:
• UI UX Pro Max: settle typography, colour and spacing. Skip when your design system already covers them.
  • threejs-web: build a rendered scene with a camera and interaction. Skip when a still image communicates as well.
  • Impeccable: critique and polish an existing interface. Start after you have a first draft.
  • Motion Design: plan timing and state transitions. Use only where movement clarifies feedback.
  • agent-browser: inspect layout and interactions when your assistant lacks browser tools.

sections.title: Start with a small pair
sections.html:
Our editorial starting pair is UI UX Pro Max plus threejs-web: visual direction and real interactive 3D. The selected 3D package is cesartevisual/threejs-skills, an independent community collection, with the exact threejs-web skill. It is distinct from CloudAI-X/threejs-skills and is not official Three.js tooling.

Use the handoff below in your website project. Read proposed changes before accepting them. These instructions are for Codex CLI; ordinary ChatGPT web chat does not acquire local skills by pasting an installer command.

sections.title: Copy this Codex handoff
sections.prompt:
Prepare this website project for a distinctive interface with real interactive 3D.
Check Codex CLI skill support, Node/npm and Python 3 first.
Read the canonical repositories and preserve existing project/config files.
Install only these two skills for this project, without global flags:
1. nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill; skill ui-ux-pro-max:
   npx ui-ux-pro-max-cli init --ai codex
2. cesartevisual/threejs-skills; skill threejs-web:
   npx skills add cesartevisual/threejs-skills --agent codex --skill threejs-web
Inspect .agents/skills and report what actually installed; reload if needed.
Do not buy services, add optional packages or change the website yet.
Ask for page purpose, audience and visual references before implementation.

sections.title: Build and check one scene
sections.html:
1. Confirm Codex sees both skills. Invoke $ui-ux-pro-max with the audience, purpose and owned references. Choose a direction before implementation.
  2. Invoke $threejs-web: "Build a rotatable lantern hero. Keep the main action in semantic HTML outside the canvas. Include loading and error states, reduced motion and a static fallback."
  3. Preview it in the browser. Rotate the object, resize the page, navigate by keyboard and try the fallback. A tilted CSS card or screenshot does not prove a 3D interaction.
  4. Ask for one targeted repair pass. Record what was exercised and what remains untested, including device/GPU coverage.

sections.title: Add only the capability you need next
sections.html:
For polish, follow Impeccable's setup: npx impeccable install --providers=codex --scope=project, reload, then $impeccable init. Review offered hooks and telemetry; its engine cache lives outside the project. Audit results still need human accessibility review.

For motion, use Motion Design: npx skills add LottieFiles/motion-design-skill, choose Codex/project scope, then $motion-design. It supplies guidance rather than requiring Lottie.

For browser checks, follow agent-browser installation: npm install agent-browser, then npx agent-browser install downloads Chrome. Its companion skill is a separate instruction layer. Existing browser tools may already suffice.

Ponytail is an optional coding-workflow companion with host adapters and hooks, outside this visual starting pair.

sections.title: A useful video companion
sections.html: The existing website tutorial provides a clear briefing and iteration pattern: brief and references - 06:02, review and polish - 15:54, mobile pass - 20:52. Our guide is an original, narrower workflow; the video's pricing, valuation and speed claims are not established here.

guides.title: Four Claude upgrades for clearer finance work
guides.description: Choose the workflow for a budget, messy export, vendor comparison or contract handoff, and practise on original synthetic files.
guides.cardSummary: Four task-specific plugins, native setup steps and a downloadable exercise with answer key.
requirements: Paid Claude access and organisation permission
Claude web or Desktop Chat for the starter route
guides.intro: Turn a spreadsheet, supplier quote or contract into a structured draft you can check. Start with one plugin that fits today's task; add others only when the next job needs them.

sections.title: Choose by the question
sections.html:
• Finance: variance analysis, reconciliation and accounting drafts. Choose it for clean accounting inputs.
  • Data: CSV/Excel profiling, SQL, charts and dashboards. Choose it before analysis when you need to understand a messy export.
  • Operations: vendor comparisons, process documentation and capacity planning. Ask for assumptions and switching effort alongside price.
  • Legal: clause references, playbook deviations and contract questions for licensed counsel. Use the result as a review handoff.

sections.title: Add Finance in Claude
sections.html:
1. Open Customize > Plugins > Discover. Find Finance by Anthropic and choose Add. Expect it to appear among your plugins. If it is missing, check the paid plan and organisation policy.
  2. Start a fresh chat. Type /, or use +, and select the variance-analysis skill. Confirm the workflow is visible before continuing.
  3. Attach the practice CSV and paste the prompt below. No bank, ERP or database connection is needed.

Official plugin help covers web Chat, Desktop Chat and Cowork. Skills and commands work in chat; hooks and sub-agents run in Cowork or Claude Code. Account sync to Code requires a supported current version. Chat access does not imply every plugin component runs there.

sections.title: Download the original practice pack
sections.html:
Download budget CSV Download answer key

Made-up values in illustrative units, created by SkillLantern on 14 November 2026. The repeated E2 row is intentional. These are exercise expectations, not observed plugin results.

sections.title: Copy this analysis prompt
sections.prompt:
Check duplicate IDs first. Show repeated rows and deduplicate identical rows only.
From sample.csv calculate budget and actual revenue, expenses and profit
(revenue minus expenses), then show absolute and percentage profit variance.
Keep the arithmetic visible. Explain only what these rows support.
List missing information; do not invent price, volume or business drivers.

sections.title: Check the answer before trusting the explanation
sections.html:
There are five raw rows, four unique rows and duplicate ID E2. Revenue is 10,000 to 11,000; expenses 6,000 to 6,500; profit 4,000 to 4,500. Profit rises 500 (+12.5%). If the result differs, check duplicate handling and the sign of expenses. These inputs do not establish price or volume drivers.

For a second exercise, download bank.csv and ledger.csv. In a fresh chat choose reconciliation and request unmatched IDs, mismatched amounts and net totals. Expected: T3 differs; bank net 500, ledger net 550; bank minus ledger -50.

sections.title: Watch the task that matches your work
sections.html: Nicolas Boucher's tutorial, published 12 November 2026: Finance - 01:20, Data - 04:42, Operations - 07:45, Legal - 08:51. Use these as demonstrations, not proof that your files or account will produce the same result.

guides.evidence: Official plugin help and all four marketplace scope pages checked 21 November 2026. Prior tutorial review used captions and sampled frames; no native installation or plugin exercise was run. Fixture arithmetic is independently checkable. Qualified finance staff should review consequential reporting; licensed counsel should review legal output. Account costs and allowances vary.
